_meta.source: TBIMS National Database public-use files (2021-10-06 release); aggregates only.
_meta.processing: 2x2 tables of people answering both questions. bothYes = a and b, aOnly = a not b, bOnly = b not a, neither. phi = (bothYes*neither - aOnly*bOnly)/sqrt(product of the four margins); t = phi*sqrt(N-2)/sqrt(1-phi^2); edge rule from BMC Neurology 2025: t above the one-tailed critical value at p < 0.01 with N-2 df.
_meta.suppression: Only pairs whose four cells are all >= 11 are exported.

pairs.role: strong positive (an edge in the published network)
pairs.note: phi = 0.48, the value quoted in BMC Neurology 2025 for depression-anxiety.

pairs.cohort: Mild TBI, 5-year follow-up, comorbidity respondents; yes = reported at all, regardless of onset
pairs.note: Same pair, counting any report of either condition.

pairs.cohort: Mild TBI, 5-year follow-up, comorbidity respondents; yes = reported at all
pairs.note: Two common conditions that simply do not travel together in this cohort: the table looks exactly like what independence predicts.

pairs.cohort: Mild TBI, 5-year follow-up, comorbidity respondents; yes = reported at all
pairs.note: Slightly fewer people with both than independence would predict; far from significant. Plausibly an age effect (cataracts in older people, depression reported more by younger people in this cohort).

pairs.cohort: All severities pooled (GCS 3-15), 5-year follow-up, comorbidity respondents; yes = reported at all. Exploratory: not a cohort used in the papers.
pairs.note: The strongest negative association with every cell >= 11. Would pass p < 0.05 but not the p < 0.01 edge rule. Almost certainly age again: ADHD is reported by younger people, hypertension by older people.
